key_points: NaOCl (0.5%–5.25%) is the most widely used endodontic irrigant; it dissolves organic tissue and has antimicrobial activity but cannot remove the smear layer or inorganic components.
EDTA (17%, pH 7) removes the smear layer but has no antibacterial properties; combined use with NaOCl reduces available chlorine and may cause dentinal erosion.
Citric acid at 10% and 1% is more effective as a decalcifying agent than 17% EDTA.
Chlorhexidine digluconate 2% has antibacterial activity but cannot dissolve necrotic tissue and is not a substitute for NaOCl.
Newer irrigants (Tetraclean, BioPure MTAD, QMix) combine chelating, antibacterial, and surfactant properties with efficacy on both organic and inorganic residues.
Laser-activated irrigation (LAI) using Er:YAG and diode lasers generates microcavitation and photoacoustic waves, increasing reaction rate, shear stress, and irrigant temperature.
PIPS™ (photon-induced photoacoustic streaming) uses Er:YAG laser at subablative power in pulsed mode to create photoacoustic waves for smear layer removal.
Both LAI and PIPS™ increase reaction rate and shear stress and reduce vapor lock effect, but carry an increased risk of apical extrusion of irrigant.
Passive ultrasonic irrigation (PUI) at 25–30 kHz increases shear stress and reaction rate with minimal risk of apical extrusion from 2 mm apex.
The EndoVac negative-pressure system reduces apical extrusion risk while improving shear stress and eliminating vapor lock; requires canal taper ≥4% and apical diameter ≥0.35 mm.
Heating NaOCl to 50°C–60°C increases its reaction rate and antibacterial efficacy without affecting canal anatomy.

NaOCl apical extrusion is a serious complication presenting with acute pain, swelling, bruising, and potential secondary infection; management includes saline irrigation, analgesics, cold/warm compresses, and possibly steroids and antibiotics.

outcomes.measured: Reaction rate of irrigant activation methods
outcomes.result: Heating, PUI, UNI, LAI, and PIPS all increase reaction rate; mechanical activation, sonic, and EndoVac do not
outcomes.clinical_significance: Increased reaction rate improves antimicrobial efficacy and organic tissue dissolution

outcomes.result: All activation methods except heating increase shear stress
outcomes.clinical_significance: Higher shear stress improves smear layer removal

outcomes.result: Mechanical activation, ultrasonic (PUI/UNI), sonic, LAI, PIPS, and EndoVac all reduce vapor lock; heating does not
outcomes.clinical_significance: Vapor lock reduction allows irrigant to reach apical third

outcomes.result: UNI, LAI, and PIPS increase apical extrusion risk; EndoVac reduces it; PUI and sonic do not influence from 2 mm apex
outcomes.clinical_significance: Apical extrusion of NaOCl can cause severe periapical tissue damage

notes: This narrative review compares multiple endodontic irrigation methods including chemical irrigants and activation techniques. Laser-related content covers LAI (Er:YAG and diode) and PIPS™ (Er:YAG subablative pulsed mode) without reporting specific laser parameters. The review does not provide numerical laser parameters (wavelength, power, pulse duration, frequency) for LAI or PIPS.

population.sample_type: Narrative review of published literature (in vitro, clinical trials, reviews)

superiority_claim: El autor afirma: 'Photoactivation techniques with cavitation lead to better results than ultrasonic methods, if used for the same amount of time, with greater removal of debris, a longer lasting and increased reaction rate, and an increased irrigant temperature.'
conflicts_of_interest: There are no conflicts of interest.
source_citation: Dioguardi, M., Di Gioia, G., Illuzzi, G., Laneve, E., Cocco, A., & Troiano, G. (2018). Endodontic irrigants: Different methods to improve efficacy and related problems. European Journal of Dentistry, 12(3), 459–466. https://doi.org/10.4103/ejd.ejd_56_18
contraindications: NaOCl irrigation with excessive pressure in teeth with wide apical foramina or destroyed apical constriction (risk of periapical extrusion)
Combined use of EDTA and NaOCl simultaneously (reduces available chlorine; NaOCl after smear layer removal causes dentinal erosion)
EndoVac system requires minimum canal taper of 4% and apical foramen diameter ≥0.35 mm; not applicable to narrower canals
adverse_events: NaOCl apical extrusion: acute pain, swelling, redness, bruising, progressive infraorbital or perioral swelling, profuse intraoral hemorrhage, facial nerve numbness/weakness, secondary infection, sinusitis, cellulitis
Accidental NaOCl injection into maxillary sinus
Accidental NaOCl injection into oral mucosa
Increased risk of apical extrusion with UNI, LAI, and PIPS techniques
clinical_indication: Root canal disinfection and smear layer removal during endodontic treatment

drugs_mentioned.name: sodium hypochlorite
drugs_mentioned.dental_relevance: Most widely used endodontic irrigant (0.5%–5.25%); dissolves organic tissue; toxic to periapical tissues if extruded; interacts with EDTA reducing available chlorine
drugs_mentioned.laser_implication: Used as irrigant activated by LAI (Er:YAG/diode) and PIPS™; laser activation increases its reaction rate and temperature

drugs_mentioned.name: ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid
drugs_mentioned.dental_relevance: Removes smear layer (inorganic component); no antibacterial activity; combined use with NaOCl reduces chlorine availability and may cause dentinal erosion

drugs_mentioned.name: chlorhexidine digluconate
drugs_mentioned.dental_relevance: Used at 2% as endodontic irrigant; antibacterial but cannot dissolve necrotic tissue; not a substitute for NaOCl; efficacy reduced by organic debris

drugs_mentioned.name: citric acid
drugs_mentioned.dental_relevance: At 10% and 1% more effective as decalcifying agent than 17% EDTA; causes slight tubule enlargement; has some antibacterial activity

drugs_mentioned.name: doxycycline hyclate
drugs_mentioned.dental_relevance: Component of Tetraclean and BioPure MTAD; used for smear layer removal and root canal disinfection
drugs_mentioned.laser_implication: Tetracyclines are photosensitizing agents; caution with laser/light activation in canals containing doxycycline-based irrigants

perioperative_consideration: NaOCl apical extrusion management: immediate saline irrigation, local/oral analgesics, cold packs for first 6h then warm compresses, steroids to minimize edema, antibiotics only if clinical evidence of wound infection or necrosis expected.
uncertainties: No specific laser parameters (wavelength, power, pulse duration, frequency, fiber type) are reported for LAI or PIPS in this narrative review; protocols are described conceptually only.
The review states LAI uses 'Er:YAG and diode lasers' without specifying which diode wavelength or whether the diode is used for photoacoustic activation or photothermal activation.
PIPS is described as using 'Er:YAG laser with subassertive power in a pulsating mode' without numerical parameters.
No specific brand or model of laser equipment is mentioned for LAI or PIPS.

bibliographic_metadata.title: Endodontic irrigants: Different methods to improve efficacy and related problems

protocols.name: Irrigación activada por láser (LAI) en endodoncia
protocols.purpose: Activar el irrigante endodóntico (NaOCl) mediante energía láser (Er:YAG o diodo) para generar microcavitación e implosión de burbujas, aumentando la tasa de reacción, el estrés de cizallamiento y la temperatura del irrigante para mejorar la desinfección y remoción del smear layer.

parameters_table.equipment_class: Cualquier Er:YAG 2940 nm o láser de diodo (810–980 nm)

critical_notes: ⚠️ Este protocolo es de carácter teórico/revisión. No se reportan parámetros clínicos numéricos específicos en este artículo. Basado en: Dioguardi et al., 2018.
LAI aumenta la tasa de reacción, el estrés de cizallamiento y reduce el efecto vapor lock, pero conlleva mayor riesgo de extrusión apical del irrigante en comparación con PUI.

El documento presenta LAI favorablemente frente a métodos ultrasónicos; existen alternativas (PUI, sónico, EndoVac) con diferentes perfiles de riesgo-beneficio que pueden ser más apropiadas según el caso clínico.
El mecanismo de acción consiste en generación de microcavitación e implosión de burbujas de irrigante por absorción rápida de energía láser.
indications: Desinfección del sistema de conductos radiculares durante tratamiento endodóntico
Remoción del smear layer en el tercio apical
Casos donde se requiere mayor tasa de reacción del irrigante
contraindications: Precaución en conductos con foramen apical amplio o constricción apical destruida (mayor riesgo de extrusión apical del irrigante)
No recomendado cuando se requiere evitar extrusión apical (considerar EndoVac en su lugar)
protocols.evidence_level: Bajo — revisión narrativa sin parámetros clínicos estandarizados ni RCTs propios. Basado en Dioguardi et al., 2018.

protocols.name: PIPS™ — Activación fotoacústica intracanal con Er:YAG subablativo
protocols.purpose: Activar el irrigante endodóntico mediante pulsos subablativos de láser Er:YAG en modo pulsado para generar ondas fotoacústicas extremadamente efectivas que remueven el smear layer y desinfectan el sistema de conductos radiculares.

parameters_table.equipment_class: Cualquier Er:YAG 2940 nm con punta radial stripped y pulsos ≤50 μs (PIPS™/activación fotoacústica)
parameters_table.fibra_punta: No especificado (punta radial stripped para PIPS™)

critical_notes: ⚠️ Este protocolo es de carácter teórico/revisión. No se reportan parámetros clínicos numéricos específicos en este artículo. Basado en: Dioguardi et al., 2018.
PIPS™ y SWEEPS™ son marcas registradas de Fotona. Otros fabricantes ofrecen técnicas fotoacústicas equivalentes con nomenclatura propia.
PIPS™ comparte con LAI el aumento de tasa de reacción y estrés de cizallamiento, pero también el mayor riesgo de extrusión apical del irrigante.
El documento presenta esta técnica favorablemente; existen alternativas (PUI, EndoVac) con menor riesgo de extrusión apical que pueden ser más apropiadas según el caso clínico.
indications: Remoción del smear layer durante tratamiento endodóntico
Desinfección del sistema de conductos radiculares
Activación de irrigantes en zonas de difícil acceso (istmos, anastomosis)
contraindications: Precaución en conductos con foramen apical amplio o constricción apical destruida (mayor riesgo de extrusión apical del irrigante)
No recomendado cuando se requiere evitar extrusión apical (considerar EndoVac en su lugar)
protocols.evidence_level: Bajo — revisión narrativa sin parámetros clínicos estandarizados ni RCTs propios. Basado en Dioguardi et al., 2018.
